correctness.summary: The growth obstruction is valid, conditional only on the stated finite-order Sklyanin/Gamma structural inputs. Smith-Tate's order-7 center has two degree-2 generators and a four-dimensional degree-7 central space. Under the compatible V4=(Z/2)^2 action, the degree-7 space is the regular V4 representation: each nonidentity two-torsion translation is fixed-point-free on the quotient elliptic curve, so holomorphic Lefschetz gives trace zero on the degree-4 section space, while the identity trace is four. Hence the Reynolds image of the four septics is one-dimensional. The explicit subalgebra C is therefore generated by at most two quadrics and one septic, so GKdim(C)<=3, whereas HS_A=(1-t)^(-4) gives GKdim(A)=4. A module-finite graded extension would have equal GK dimension, so A cannot be finite over this C. This does not decide PI-finiteness over the full center.

limitations: The proof uses the established Smith-Tate finite-order center description and the compatible two-torsion action; those general structure theorems are not reproved in the record.
The conclusion refutes finiteness over the named Reynolds-generated subalgebra C only; it does not determine A's full center, PI degree, or rank over that center.
The regular-representation conclusion uses the equivariant degree-4 line-bundle model on the quotient elliptic curve and fixed-point-free nonidentity two-torsion translations.
Literature search non-detection is not a priority or novelty proof.

originality.summary: Finite-order Sklyanin centers, the exotic elliptic invariant algebra, and the two-torsion action are established literature. The audited contribution is the explicit observation that the particular Reynolds-generated Smith-Tate subalgebra collapses to at most three generators and therefore cannot support the proposed finite-module route. A focused search did not locate this exact obstruction, but search non-detection is not treated as proof of priority.

scientific_value.summary: The result decisively rules out the target's proposed explicit central subalgebra and rank computation by a short representation-theoretic and growth argument. It narrows the viable PI analysis without claiming to determine the true full center or PI degree of the exotic algebra.
